diagnoses.description: SKILL.md claims the skill is for D3.js (v6) in the header/front matter, but later instructs to pin D3 to v7.9.0 by default, creating an internal version inconsistency that can mislead implementations needing v6.

bubble_chart_example.js uses an absolute data path (d3.csv('/data/stocks.csv')), which is brittle for standalone apps opened from disk and contradicts the common need for relative paths within the output tree.

bubble_chart_example.js tooltip suppression for ETFs is implemented as `if (d.sector !== 'ETF')`, but ETF-ness is not reliably represented by the `sector` field; the example simultaneously computes `hasValue`/missing marketCap but does not use it for tooltip gating, which is logically inconsistent and encourages incorrect behavior.

locations.section: Data parsing (hasValue) vs. circle mouseover handler (sector !== 'ETF')

diagnoses.description: SKILL.md instructs users to import a `dialogue_graph` module (`from dialogue_graph import Graph, Node, Edge`), but the bundle only provides `dialogue-graph/scripts/dialogue_graph.py` and does not define an installable/importable `dialogue_graph` package/module at the documented import path. diagnoses.description: `Graph.validate()` is advertised as validating graph integrity, but it only checks edge endpoint existence and does not validate key constraints that the task/evaluators commonly enforce (e.g., all nodes reachable from the first node). Using this validation as-is can allow structurally invalid graphs to pass "validate" while failing downstream constraints.

The implementation treats the special target `"End"` inconsistently across validation/serialization/visualization: `validate()` explicitly allows edges to point to `End` even when `End` is not present in `self.nodes`, `to_dict()`/`to_json()` will omit an `End` node unless the user added one, but `visualize()` always injects an `End` node into the DOT output. This can produce a JSON graph with dangling `to: "End"` references (depending on consumer expectations) and a DOT graph that does not faithfully represent the serialized JSON graph.

`senior-data-engineer/scripts/data_quality_validator.py` has a broken CLI wiring: `DataQualityValidator.__init__` expects a single `config: Dict`, but `main()` instantiates it with `(args.target, verbose=...)`, and then calls `tool.run()` even though the class only defines `process()` (no `run()` method). This will raise `TypeError`/`AttributeError` and makes the script unusable as documented.

locations.section: class DataQualityValidator.__init__ signature vs main(): tool instantiation and tool.run() call

diagnoses.description: `time_above_threshold_s` treats “above threshold” as strictly `>` (not `>=`), which will undercount TAL when temperatures equal the threshold (e.g., at liquidus). It also fails to count segments where both endpoints equal the threshold (flat-at-threshold dwell). This is a concrete computation defect because the function’s logic omits equality cases rather than making the comparison operator configurable.

diagnoses.description: `save-plan` claims it "Uses `unified_planning.io.PDDLWriter`" to write a plan in "standard PDDL plan format". `PDDLWriter` is for emitting PDDL domain/problem text, not serializing a computed plan into a plain action-per-line plan file. This is likely to produce the wrong output format or fail at runtime, and it does not align with the task requirement of writing a textual plan (one action per line) to `plan_output`.

The plan-generation notes hard-code the default planner as `pyperplan`, but `pyperplan` is commonly limited to STRIPS-style fragments and may not support typical IPC Airport encodings that use richer PDDL requirements (e.g., ADL features, conditional effects, negative/disjunctive preconditions). This makes the documented default approach unreliable for the stated benchmark suite.
